name: THE WATCHMAN'S SHACK
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE COT
LOOK_AT: A cot. It has never been slept in.
The blanket is folded square, with corners you could rule a ledger by. Somebody learned that a long way from here.
There is no dent in the pillow. A man who works nights must sleep days, and he does not do it here.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Not a rope under it has been asked to take a weight in years.
Nothing. A cot that has never been slept in has never learned to creak.

overrides.USE: It has been made, military-fashion, every day for years, and slept in — by the look of it — almost never.

subjects.name: THE TALLY MARKS
LOOK_AT: Marks cut into the wall. Thousands of them. Someone has been counting something here for a very long time and has not stopped.
In fives, the fifth stroke always across. Every group is finished except the last, which is today's.
The oldest are at the height of a standing man's eye and gone soft with handling. The newest are down by the floor. He has run out of wall.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The knife that made these is not here, and neither is the man.
I put my ear to the boards. Wood, and the street beyond it. Nobody is counting out loud.

subjects.name: THE LAMP
LOOK_AT: Trimmed, filled, and ready. It is the only well-maintained object I have seen in Consolation.
The wick is trimmed square, and the glass is polished on the inside, which is the side that matters and the side nobody checks.
The brass is worn bright in one place, where a hand lifts it the same way every evening.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It is waiting for dark, and it is good at waiting.
Not a sound. It is the only thing in this room that expects to be needed tonight.

subjects.name: THE COAT ON THE NAIL
LOOK_AT: A coat. Eastern cut, twelve or thirteen years out of fashion, and far too good for a night watchman.
The lining is silk, worn through at one pocket, where something heavy was carried for a long time.
It has been brushed recently and not worn in years. Somebody looks after it for no reason I can see.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Good wool keeps quiet on principle.
Nothing. It hangs exactly straight. Even the draft has been asked to leave it alone.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW
LOOK_AT: It faces Main Street. It faces the Improvement Company. Whoever put this window in wanted to see one particular building.
The glass has been cleaned in one square only, at the height of a man on a stool. The rest of the window may do as it likes.
From here you can see every door on Main Street, and the Company's twice. I do not know what you would be watching for. I suspect he does.
LISTEN_TO: Main Street, at the distance a watchman would choose: near enough to hear a door, far enough not to be asked anything.
The Company's door, opening and closing. From in here it is the loudest thing in town.

subjects.name: THE STOVE
LOOK_AT: Cold. It has not been lit this season.
Swept out, and the ash bucket empty. A cold stove that someone still cleans.
There is kindling laid in it, dry, and from the dust on it, laid a long time ago.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Iron, at the temperature of the room, which is the temperature of outside.
Nothing. A stove that has given up on this season and possibly the next.

HOB.PICK_UP: No. Some men you leave exactly where they have chosen to stand.
HOB.PUSH: He has stood in one place for twelve years. I am not going to be the one who moves him.
HOB.USE: No. Everybody in this town has had some use of him, and none of them noticed. I will not make one more.

THE DOOR.CLOSE: It doesn't latch from outside. A watchman's door. Nothing of his was ever protected but the town.
